rationale: The story turns on one physical object—the vent screen—and the millimeter-scale difference in mesh openings that determines ember passage. A 100mm macro close-up makes the openings legible and turns the ember leak into a visible, tactile threat.

core_thesis: The compliant 1/8-inch vent screen that homeowners are told to install is the one laboratory testing found still passes burning embers, making it the one hardening item where discount eligibility knowingly selects the weaker mesh.
core_conflict: The state's insurance-discount list and fire councils accept the 1/8-inch mesh size while laboratory testing shows embers passing through it still ignite attic fuel, versus the finer 1/16-inch screen that blocks more embers but reduces airflow.
